rules.description: The service layer must not depend directly on a persistence implementation (JDBC, JPA or Spring Data JPA classes); it must use the repository interfaces.
rules.rationale: The readme documents three interchangeable persistence implementations selected by Spring profile. A direct service-to-implementation dependency would tie the service to one implementation and break that documented design.

rules.description: Controllers (REST controllers in rest, or Spring MVC controllers in web) must not depend directly on the persistence layer (repository interfaces or implementations); they must go through the service layer.
rules.rationale: The readme layer table orders REST API controllers above the Service layer. The project history states the rule explicitly: commit a994785f73a848058a4bad7b5bb2ef00f1b2fa2c 'made sure the ClinicService facade is used by all Controllers'. The rule requires controllers to go through the service layer, so it applies only when a service layer exists (requires_layers). Before commit c9c8c4e there was no service layer and controllers used the Clinic data-access interface directly by design.

rules.description: Model (domain entity) classes must not depend on the presentation, service or persistence layers.
rules.rationale: Entities are shared by every layer; a dependency from model to a higher layer would create a cycle between layers.

class_mapping_evidence.evidence: Root-package entity classes (2013-01-09..2013-02-13). Annotated @Entity/@MappedSuperclass (Vets: @XmlRootElement); commit 23314c5 'moved all model classes to a dedicated model package' moved exactly these.

Root-package Clinic interface ('Retrieve ... from the data store'), implemented by the jdbc/jpa/hibernate Clinic classes; replaced by the repository interfaces in commit c9c8c4e 'moved the ClinicRepository into some separate repos'.

Spring MVC controllers in the early sample modules (annotated @Controller), and form-backing objects bound by those controllers (*Form). Existed until commit 87ccf9f 'first step of migration to Spring 3.2'.
class_mapping_evidence.ambiguity: appointments.AppointmentForm is also used by the AppointmentBook repository interface; checked that classifying it as model instead changes no rule result.

In-memory repository implementations in the early sample modules, annotated @Repository.
Plain domain classes in the early sample modules (no framework annotations; fields + accessors).
